newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU and U.S. hold new talks on drug product recognition.
newsitem.headline: EU and U.S. hold new talks on drug product recognition.

text.p: The European Union made fresh proposals to the United States Tuesday in a bid to complete recently stalled talks over simplifying trade in pharmaceutical and other medical products, EU officials said.

EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan submitted the proposals to U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky at private talks on the sidelines of a meeting of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, they said.
No details of the proposals were made available and a U.S. official said no agreement was expected to be reached soon.

Despite a stalemate in Washington talks last week, Brittan hoped to clinch an agreement soon so that pharmaceutical, medical and other products certified in the European Union will not need double-checking in the United States and vice-versa, EU officials said.

They said they had reached agreement on this so-called mutual recognition mechanism as far as telecommunications products, such as telephones and computers, were concerned and also on small electrical equipment, such as kitchen appliances.
But the sticking points proved to be pharmaceutical products and medical devices.
EU officials said the U.S. Food and Drugs Administration was reluctant to give up its powers to approve or reject European products.

One U.S. official close to last week's talks said that from the U.S. point of view the main sticking points were the EU demands on testing and certification of pharmaceuticals products and medical equipment, which the United States believed would lower U.S. consumer standards.
